title: DF Bus Workers Suspend Strike After Wage Agreement
seoTitle: DF Bus Workers Suspend Strike After Wage Deal
subtitle: The walkout approaching the election was canceled with an 8% wage increase and 10% in benefits
excerpt: The Federal District bus workers' strike was suspended after a deal securing an 8% wage increase and a 10% raise in food benefits.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: G1, Correio Braziliense, Diário do Poder
contentHtml:
The Federal District bus workers' strike, scheduled to begin in the early hours of September 28, was called off after an agreement between the union, bus companies, and the DF Department of Mobility. The deal secures an 8% wage increase and 10% in food benefits, such as meal vouchers and food baskets.

What changed in the agreement

The union had demanded an 8% wage increase, 10% for food allowances, and 12% for health insurance. The final proposal, accepted by all parties, included 8% for wages and 10% for food benefits, with no changes to the health plan.

Impact on the fleet and commuters

Companies confirmed that the fleet is expected to operate normally in the early hours of Monday morning, with buses running without interruptions. The Labor Court had ruled that, should the strike continue, the fleet would have to operate at 80% during peak hours, 50% during off-peak hours, and 100% on voting days, subject to a fine of up to R$ 200,000 per hour in the event of non-compliance.

Political and electoral context

The strike was set to take place ahead of the October 4 elections, when public transit would be halted. The DF government labeled the walkout as political and election-driven, claiming the strike could be used to undermine the local administration. The deal prevents public transit from being disrupted during the voting period.

Reaction from the government and the union

Celina Leão, DF governor, posted on X that the suspension of the strike was "excellent news" and that the agreement was reached through the mediation of the Department of Mobility and the DF Attorney General's Office. João Dâo, director of the DF Land Transport Workers Union, stated that the agreement guarantees an 8% wage increase and 10% in benefits.

Future outlook

The agreement was signed during a meeting on Sunday night (Sept. 27). A meeting on Monday (28) is set to define the exact terms of the negotiation. The companies have not yet detailed whether the amounts will be paid as early as October. The Labor Court upheld the right to strike, but established minimum operating requirements in the event of any future walkout.

With reporting from G1, Correio Braziliense, Diário do Poder.
